answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate and 14-day expiration create urgency, but the 94% volume buffer and critical-line status demand protection against delivery risk. Switching to the low-cost vendor (memory_c2) is ruled out—they missed SLA three of four quarters and cannot be sole source on critical lines. Deferring past renewal is not viable with no auto-renew clause. Renewing without negotiation forgoes the margin recovery demonstrated in memory_c4. Adding a second source (memory_c3) is the safest tactical move for resilience, but the real cost lever is renegotiation: memory_c4 shows benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and terms, and memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing. The optimal play is to negotiate_terms with the incumbent now, targeting the 18% reduction through a combination of volume pricing and payment restructuring (as demonstrated in c4 and c6), while preserving the incumbent relationship and delivery reliability. This protects against SLA risk on the constrained line while meeting the financial mandate. Verification of c2 and c4 will confirm the SLA gap and the negotiation leverage respectively.
